name: Question 4
problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ as a function of $t.$
worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & ={e}^{-t}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & ={e}^{-t}\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{-t}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & ={e}^{-t}\sqrt{2({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{2}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-2{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =2{e}^{-t}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =({e}^{-t}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩)\times (2{e}^{-t}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0⟩) \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}\,\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}({cos}^{2}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)k \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=2{e}^{-2t}.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{-2t}}{{(\sqrt{2}{e}^{-t})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{-2t}}{2\sqrt{2}{e}^{-3t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{t}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of r(t)=⟨e−tcos⁡t,e−tsin⁡t⟩ as a function of t.

a
2et2
b
2et
c
e−t
d
e−t2
e
2et
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The curvature κ is given by κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t) and ‖r′(t)‖: r′(t)=⟨ddt(e−tcos⁡t),ddt(e−tsin⁡t)⟩=⟨−e−tcos⁡t−e−tsin⁡t,e−tcos⁡t−e−tsin⁡t⟩=e−t⟨−cos⁡t−sin⁡t,cos⁡t−sin⁡t⟩‖r′(t)‖=e−t(−cos⁡t−sin⁡t)2+(cos⁡t−sin⁡t)2=e−tcos2⁡t+2sin⁡tcos⁡t+sin2⁡t+cos2⁡t−2sin⁡tcos⁡t+sin2⁡t=e−t2(cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t)=2e−t

Now, we find the second derivative: r″(t)=⟨ddt(−e−tcos⁡t−e−tsin⁡t),ddt(e−tcos⁡t−e−tsin⁡t)⟩=⟨2e−tsin⁡t,−2e−tcos⁡t⟩=2e−t⟨sin⁡t,−cos⁡t⟩

Next, we compute the cross product by considering r′(t) and r″(t) as 3-dimensional vectors with zero z-components: r′(t)×r″(t)=(e−t⟨−cos⁡t−sin⁡t,cos⁡t−sin⁡t,0⟩)×(2e−t⟨sin⁡t,−cos⁡t,0⟩)=2e−2tijk−cos⁡t−sin⁡tcos⁡t−sin⁡t0sin⁡t−cos⁡t0=2e−2t−cos⁡t−sin⁡tcos⁡t−sin⁡tsin⁡t−cos⁡tk=2e−2t(cos2⁡t+sin⁡tcos⁡t−sin⁡tcos⁡t+sin2⁡t)k=2e−2tk

So, the magnitude of the cross product is ‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖=2e−2t.

Therefore, the curvature is κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3=2e−2t(2e−t)3=2e−2t22e−3t=2et2.
